statement: AI should never be listed as an author, because it cannot take responsibility for the work.
PhD students and postdocs face the biggest career risk when AI solves the open problems they work on.
Publish-or-perish incentives, not AI itself, are the main cause of the flood of low-quality papers.
The real goal of science is human understanding, not just correct answers.
A result with no human author should still count as a real scientific contribution.
Science should deliberately slow down in the age of AI, even if it means fewer discoveries.
Reviewers should be allowed to use AI to help write their peer reviews.
Scientists who check and explain AI companies' results are doing free labor for those companies.
Rules for AI in science should be set by the public, not just by scientists and publishers.
Within 10 years, most new scientific findings will come from AI agents, not human scientists.
